title: Microsoft Purview: auto-expanding archive limit rises from 1.5 TB to 3 TB for eligible mailboxes
summary: The briefing's capacity limits, eligible licensing, automatic rollout and PowerShell controls are supported by Microsoft's notice and current Learn documentation. The roadmap metadata matches the record, and the briefing correctly distinguishes the updated 3 TB notice from Learn's remaining 1.5 TB body text.

claims.claim: The body of Learn about auto-expanding archiving still describes a 1.5 TB maximum in November 2026.
claims.quote: This archiving feature in Microsoft Purview (called auto-expanding archiving) provides up to 1.5 TB of additional storage in archive mailboxes.

claims.claim: The body of Enable auto-expanding archiving still describes a 1.5 TB maximum in November 2026.
claims.quote: When auto-expanding archiving is turned on, additional storage space is automatically added to a user's archive mailbox until it reaches the storage limit of 1.5 TB.

claims.claim: Auto-expanding archiving supports a mailbox growth rate that does not exceed 1 GB per day.
claims.quote: Auto-expanding archiving is supported only for mailboxes used by individual users or for shared mailboxes with a growth rate that doesn't exceed 1 GB per day.

claims.claim: Eligible users gain additional archive headroom without a support request.
claims.quote: This enhancement helps organizations retain and manage larger volumes of archived email content without requiring manual archive expansion processes or support requests.

claims.claim: eDiscovery tools such as Content Search search the additional storage areas of auto-expanded archives.
claims.quote: When you use an eDiscovery tool, such as Content Search, the additional storage areas in an auto-expanded archive are also searched.

claims.claim: Putting a mailbox on hold also places content in its auto-expanded archive on hold.
claims.quote: When you put a mailbox on hold by using methods such as Microsoft 365 retention, eDiscovery case holds, and Litigation Hold in Exchange Online, content located in an auto-expanded archive is also placed on hold.

claims.claim: The capacity increase describes no new permission or identity.
claims.quote: Searched: auto-expanding archive 3 TB new permissions identity roles. Read MC1472592 and Learn's enable-autoexpanding-archiving and autoexpanding-archiving pages; the increase names no new permission or identity.

claims.claim: Learn's archive pages state no price for moving a user to an eligible license.
claims.quote: Searched: site:learn.microsoft.com/purview/enable-autoexpanding-archiving price upgrade eligible license 3 TB. Read enable-autoexpanding-archiving and autoexpanding-archiving in full; neither states an upgrade price.

claims.claim: Auto-expanding archiving supports shared mailboxes.
claims.quote: Auto-expanding archiving also supports shared mailboxes.

claims.claim: The user's archive mailbox must be enabled before enabling auto-expanding archiving.
claims.quote: A user's mailbox must already be enabled for archive before you can enable auto-expanding archiving.

claims.claim: Auto-expanding archiving supports cloud archive mailboxes in an Exchange hybrid deployment.
claims.quote: Auto-expanding archiving is supported for cloud-based archive mailboxes in an Exchange hybrid deployment for users who have an on-premises primary mailbox.

claims.claim: Auto-expanding archiving is not supported for on-premises mailboxes.
claims.quote: Auto-expanding archiving isn't supported for on-premises mailboxes in any version of Exchange Server.

claims.claim: Enabling auto-expanding archiving requires Exchange Online PowerShell, not the Exchange admin center or Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.quote: You can't use the Exchange admin center or the Microsoft Purview portal to enable auto-expanding archiving. You must use Exchange Online PowerShell.

claims.claim: No admin UI path is documented for enabling organization-wide auto-expanding archiving.
claims.quote: Searched: auto-expanding archiving enable Exchange admin center Microsoft Purview portal UI. Read enable-autoexpanding-archiving: it explicitly excludes both portals and requires Exchange Online PowerShell.

claims.claim: No admin UI path is documented for enabling auto-expanding archiving for a specific user.
claims.quote: Searched: auto-expanding archiving enable Exchange admin center Microsoft Purview portal UI. Read enable-autoexpanding-archiving: it explicitly excludes both portals and documents the per-user PowerShell command.

claims.claim: Set-OrganizationConfig -AutoExpandingArchive enables auto-expanding archiving for the whole organization in Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote: To enable auto-expanding archiving for your entire organization, run the following command: Set-OrganizationConfig -AutoExpandingArchive

claims.claim: Enable-Mailbox <user mailbox> -AutoExpandingArchive enables auto-expanding archiving for a specific user in Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote: To enable auto-expanding archiving for a specific user, run the following command. Enable-Mailbox <user mailbox> -AutoExpandingArchive

claims.claim: The per-user Enable-Mailbox -AutoExpandingArchive command requires cloud-based primary and archive mailboxes.
claims.quote: If a user's primary and archive mailboxes are both cloud-based, then you can use the Enable-Mailbox -AutoExpandingArchive command to enable auto-expanding archiving for that specific user.

claims.claim: For an on-premises primary mailbox with a cloud archive, use Set-OrganizationConfig -AutoExpandingArchive rather than the per-user command.
claims.quote: To enable auto-expanding archiving for cloud-based archive mailboxes in an Exchange hybrid deployment, you have to run the Set-OrganizationConfig -AutoExpandingArchive command in Exchange Online PowerShell to enable auto-expanding archiving for the entire organization.

claims.claim: Get-OrganizationConfig | FL AutoExpandingArchiveEnabled checks the organization's auto-expanding archiving state.
claims.quote: To verify that auto-expanding archiving is enabled for your organization, run the following command in Exchange Online PowerShell. Get-OrganizationConfig | FL AutoExpandingArchiveEnabled

claims.claim: Get-Mailbox <user mailbox> | FL AutoExpandingArchiveEnabled checks a specific user's auto-expanding archiving state.
claims.quote: To verify that auto-expanding archiving is enabled for a specific user, run the following command in Exchange Online PowerShell. Get-Mailbox <user mailbox> | FL AutoExpandingArchiveEnabled

claims.claim: Organization-wide enablement does not change AutoExpandingArchiveEnabled on individual user mailboxes to True.
claims.quote: Running the Set-OrganizationConfig cmdlet to enable auto-expanding archiving for your organization doesn't change the AutoExpandingArchiveEnabled property on user mailboxes to True.

claims.claim: Enabling auto-expanding archiving for a specific user on hold or assigned a retention policy adds 10 GB to the primary archive quota.
claims.quote: The storage quota for the user's primary archive mailbox is increased by 10 GB (from 100 GB to 110 GB).

claims.claim: Learn's archive pages do not say what happens to an archive above 1.5 TB if its eligible license is subsequently removed.
claims.quote: Searched: auto expanding archive 3 TB eligible license removed downgrade 1.5 TB. Read enable-autoexpanding-archiving and autoexpanding-archiving in full; neither describes an over-1.5-TB archive after license removal.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends reviewing license assignments for users with large archive mailboxes.
claims.quote: Review license assignments for users with large archive mailboxes to confirm eligibility.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends updating internal documentation, retention guidance and help desk materials for the 3 TB limit.
claims.quote: Update internal documentation, retention guidance, and help desk materials to reflect the new 3 TB limit.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends reviewing licensing and retention strategies for users not eligible for expanded capacity.
claims.quote: Review licensing and retention strategies for users whose archive mailboxes are not eligible for the expanded capacity.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn says that no more data is stored in an auto-expanding archive once the documented 1.5 TB limit is reached, relevant to licenses retaining that limit.
claims.quote: If a mailbox with an auto-expanding archive reaches a total of 1.5 TB of data stored in the auto-expanding archive, no more data will be stored in the auto-expanding archive or moved from the main archive to the auto-expanding archive.

controlChecks.governs: Auto-expanding archiving for the whole organisation
